name: Rainbow Serpent (Ngalyod)
role: A living creator serpent of waterholes, rain and law, called Ngalyod in Kuninjku and Kunwinjku country of western Arnhem Land.
fun_fact: In Kuninjku accounts she sheds her skin to renew herself, and the roar of a waterfall is said to be her voice.

name: Seven Sisters
role: Ancestral women of the Western Desert, the Pleiades, whose journey is sung across Warlpiri, Pitjantjatjara, Yankunytjatjara and Ngaanyatjarra country.
fun_fact: Their songline crosses more than half the continent, and different language groups hold and care for different sections of it.

name: Baiame
role: The sky creator of the Wiradjuri and Kamilaroi peoples of inland New South Wales, who made the land, the first people and the law.
fun_fact: His name is spelled Baiame, Biame, Biami, Baayami and Byamee in different records, and some of his sites are closed men's ceremonial places.

name: Wandjina
role: Rain-bringing creator ancestors of the Kimberley, painted in rock shelters across Worrorra, Ngarinyin and Wunambal country and repainted to renew the land.
fun_fact: Wandjina are painted with eyes and a nose but no mouth, and the lines around the head are read as the lightning before the wet season.

name: Bunyip
role: A water being of south-eastern Australia whose English name comes from Wemba-Wemba or Wergaia country and now covers many different nations' stories.
fun_fact: A skull exhibited as a bunyip's in the 1840s was later identified as that of a deformed horse.

name: Emu (Dinewan)
role: The emu ancestor of the Euahlayi people of northern New South Wales, recorded as Dinewan, a trickster and the husband of the crows.
fun_fact: In Parker's 1896 telling, Dinewan is burned with hot coals by his crow wives after he keeps kicking the bark off their shelter.

name: Crow (Wahn)
role: The crow of Euahlayi story, one of the two wives of Dinewan the emu in K. Langloh Parker's 1896 record.
fun_fact: In Kulin country to the south the crow is Waa, brother of Bunjil the eaglehawk, which is a different relationship from the Euahlayi story.

name: Kangaroo
role: A key animal of Country in many nations, painted beside the Wandjina in Kimberley shelters and known by different names in different languages.
fun_fact: Kimberley rock shelters carry kangaroo figures beside the Wandjina, and Kuninjku artists give Ngalyod the ears of a kangaroo.

name: Bunjil the Eaglehawk
role: The creator eaglehawk of the Kulin nations of Victoria, whose brother is Waa the crow and whose story is distinct from Baiame and the Wandjina.
fun_fact: Bunjil is honoured across Kulin country, and Wurundjeri and Boonwurrung people tell of him alongside Waa the crow.

name: Waterhole
role: A permanent water place in Country, understood in many nations as a living site with its own law, its own keeper and sometimes a serpent beneath it.
fun_fact: In Kuninjku country a waterhole may be the Rainbow Serpent's home, and who may swim or fish there is part of the law of that place.
